rounds.text: Sunraj Diamond Exports is demonstrating a significant operational turnaround [E64], evidenced by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 200% [E20] and a 91% year-on-year increase in sales [E56]. This momentum is supported by a dramatic 45 percentage point improvement in quarterly operating margins [E30] and the generation of Rs 2.09 Cr in both operating and free cash flow as of March 2026 [E34, E35]. The company is also strengthening its balance sheet by reducing total borrowings [E38], while the fact that recent profit growth has exceeded price growth by 230% [E47] suggests the market has yet to recognize these fundamental improvements [E64]. Conceded: the company currently trades at an exceptionally high P/E of 333x [E1], maintains a high debt-to-equity ratio of 15.78x [E36], and reports a negative return on equity of -6.2% [E13]. However, with sales growth accelerating to 33% in the trailing twelve months [E17] and a results score of 84/100 [E64], the business appears to be outperforming expectations despite its historically low return on equity [E52, E61].

Sunraj Diamond Exports Ltd is dangerously overvalued, trading at a P/E of 333x and a P/B of 7.18x, which is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 1.99x [E1, E2, E7]. The company’s financial health is precarious, evidenced by a massive debt-to-equity ratio of 15.78x and a low interest coverage ratio [E36, E50]. Profitability remains deeply negative or negligible, with a trailing twelve-month operating margin of -14% and a return on equity of -5.88% [E29, E9]. Furthermore, promoter confidence appears to be waning as their holding has dropped from 41.27% to 35.83% [E40]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth shows a 200% increase and sales grew by 33% [E20, E17], yet these improvements do not justify a price that is 566% above its DCF-calculated intrinsic value [E44]. The stock's current price implies an aggressive 48.3% earnings growth rate that far exceeds the 15% base case assumption [E45].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E7, E36, E44, E45]. While the bear highlights rich valuation multiples and high leverage, the bear ignores that borrowings have actively decreased from Rs 16.75 Cr to Rs 14.68 Cr [E38]. Conceded: [E9, E29]. However, dismissing the business on past profitability ignores a powerful operational inflection: quarterly operating margin surged by 45 percentage points year-over-year in June 2026 [E30]. Furthermore, the company generated positive free cash flow of Rs 2.09 Cr in March 2026 [E35], directly contradicting the notion that the business lacks cash-generation capabilities. Conceded: [E40]. Finally, the bear's reliance on stale sentiment overlooks the fact that results are actively improving with a high results score and sector-matching growth acceleration, making current pessimism a lagging indicator [E20, E47, E64].

Conceded: [E38]. While borrowings have indeed decreased from Rs 16.75 Cr to Rs 14.68 Cr [E38], a debt-to-equity ratio of 15.78x still means debt vastly exceeds net worth, leaving the business severely leveraged [E36]. Conceded: [E30, E35]. Although quarterly operating margin showed a one-quarter surge [E30] and the company produced positive free cash flow of Rs 2.09 Cr [E35], the operating margin over the trailing twelve months remains deep in negative territory at -14% [E29]. Pointing to an isolated quarterly margin expansion [E30] or a single year of cash generation [E35] ignores the multi-year reality of a median 10-year ROE of -33% [E25] and a 3-year median ROE of -6% [E27]. Furthermore, dismissing current pessimism as a lagging indicator [E64] overlooks the harsh fundamentals: a steep P/E of 333x [E1], a negative ROCE of -1.3% [E12], and a reverse DCF price that requires an unrealistic 48.3% earnings growth to justify today's valuation [E45]. Finally, promoter holding continues to erode, dropping to 35.83% [E40], reinforcing that insiders are reducing their stake rather than endorsing any alleged turnaround story.
